subject.declared_domain: NFRA_GLOBGRPH -- the INCREMENTAL local Kuzu-projection refresh, the local analog of the cloud incremental_updater Lambda (Andrew-directed 2026-07-08). Applies ONLY the delta between the canonical DB's pinned snapshot and the new Nessie HEAD -- MERGE changed/added nodes, DETACH DELETE removed ones, MERGE/DELETE edges -- on a FILE-COPY, so _canonical's mutex and atomic swap are untouched. Signals FALLBACK when the delta approximates a full-table overwrite, letting the caller run the full kuzu_nessie_load instead.

as_of.graph_vintage: Holds no vintage of its own; it pins per-run to the same branch-head marker as subjects 2 and 3, measured live this session at 2026-08-30T02:11:47Z. It STAMPS a vintage via _provenance.write_manifest on a successful incremental apply, carrying the HEAD snapshot ids it just diffed against.

methodology.how: A subprocess entry point. _read_head_tables pins to the branch-head marker (RAISING if the marker cannot be resolved -- incremental requires a deterministic pin) and reads both Iceberg tables whole. The pure diff+apply core takes head data as PARAMETERS so it is unit-testable without Iceberg or cloud access: it opens the live canonical DB READ-ONLY, reads {key: snapshot_ts} and the edge identity map, releases the handle, then computes node upserts (absent or snapshot_ts-changed) and deletes (present locally, absent from HEAD). If the node delta is both >= FALLBACK_MIN_ABS (4000) AND >= FALLBACK_FRACTION (0.25) of head, it returns 'fallback' unapplied. Otherwise it FILE-COPIES the DB to a tmp path, applies in the order delete-edges, DETACH-DELETE-nodes, upsert-nodes, upsert-edges, then runs a post-apply guard and stamps a manifest. Exit codes are the caller's signal: 0 incremental applied, 2 fallback, 1 error; on any non-zero the tmp is removed so the caller's full reload starts clean.

key.identity_space: TWO identities, both deliberately mirrored from kuzu_nessie_load. NODE identity is the Kuzu PK; EDGE identity is the 4-tuple the full loader MERGEs on, and I verified both expressions are character-for-character the same rule as the full loader's. ⚠ SCOPE OF THAT CLAIM, stated because the obvious wider version is false: matching key rules means the two paths cannot diverge ON KEY CONSTRUCTION. It does NOT mean the resulting DBs cannot diverge -- the incremental path applies a delta to an existing projection while the full path rebuilds from source, and the post-apply count guard exists precisely because they CAN differ for reasons that have nothing to do with the key rule.

Dedup keeps the highest snapshot_ts per key (:57-59). EDGE IDENTITY, :185: the 4-tuple (src_id, dst_id, edge_type or '', props or '') -- raw src_id/dst_id with no strip and no fallback, matching the full loader's edge handling exactly, INCLUDING its asymmetry with the node rule. failure_mode.returns_on_failure: FAIL-SAFE BY REFUSAL, AND THE REFUSALS ARE THE DESIGN. Four distinct refusal paths, each leaving the canonical DB untouched: (1) an unresolvable marker RAISES (:72-74) rather than proceeding on an unpinned HEAD; (2) a large delta returns 'fallback' UNAPPLIED with the reason and the changed-count in stats (:173-176); (3) a post-apply guard compares node and edge counts against the HEAD sets and, on mismatch, DELETES the tmp and returns 'fallback' (:224-231); (4) any unexpected exception in main() is caught, PRINTS its type and message to stderr, and sets rc=1 (:340-342), with the tmp removed in the finally block so the caller's full reload starts clean. Exit codes 0/2/1 are the caller's contract and _canonical falls through to the full loader on 2 or 1 -- so every failure degrades to the MORE EXPENSIVE BUT CORRECT path rather than to a wrong DB. The four local except-handlers are all in _rm_kuzu / _copy_kuzu cleanup and all 'pass' on OSError, which cannot mask a data defect. ⛔ THE ONE CLAIM THAT NEEDS NARROWING IS THE MODULE'S OWN: its docstring says the guard means 'never swap in a wrong DB' (:26). What is implemented is a CARDINALITY check -- rn != len(head_keys) or re_ != len(head_edge_set) -- and equal counts do not mean equal membership. A compensating pair (one node wrongly deleted and one wrongly added in the same run) passes the guard. 'Never swap in a wrong-CARDINALITY DB' is the property that exists.
silent_degrade_paths: the post-apply guard is a COUNT comparison, not a content or checksum comparison (:224-231), so a compensating error pair -- equal numbers of wrong deletions and wrong additions -- passes it and is swapped in

verdict.why: On the evidence I measured, this is the most carefully failure-engineered subject on the face, and the credits below are scoped to exactly what I read rather than generalised from it. It refuses in four distinct ways and every refusal leaves the canonical DB untouched: it RAISES on an unresolvable pin rather than proceeding, returns FALLBACK unapplied when the delta approximates a full overwrite, deletes its own tmp and falls back when a post-apply check disagrees, and converts any unexpected exception into rc=1 with the type and message printed. Every one of those degrades to the more expensive FULL RELOAD path rather than swapping in its own partial result. ⚠ The credit is that it hands off rather than guesses -- NOT that the destination is correct: the full loader is subject 2 on this face and carries its own QUALIFIED verdict, so 'degrades to the full path' is what I measured and 'degrades to a correct result' is not mine to assert here. Its four local except-handlers are confined to filesystem cleanup and all pass on OSError, so none can mask a data defect. It mirrors the full loader's node key and edge identity character-for-character, so the two paths cannot diverge on KEY CONSTRUCTION -- which is narrower than 'cannot produce different DBs', a claim the post-apply guard's own existence contradicts -- and its _cur_edges comparand carries the SET-fields specifically to catch an in-place re-layer that identity-only matching would miss -- a named drift vector closed in code rather than left to an oracle. It prints both sides of every delta, so the ratio its fallback gate turns on is reconstructible from the log alone. QUALIFIED on two measured defects. FIRST, A DECLARATIVE DRIFT WHOSE TWO HALVES ARE BOTH STALE: the docstring says this path is 'Gated OFF by default ... pending CTO arch-gate of the design', while its only caller records 'DEFAULT-ON', cites the arch-gate GO at 195732Z, and states the flag was deliberately flipped opt-IN to DEFAULT after the 2026-07-09 graph-infra incident. The environment variable is unset on this box, so the caller's default applies and this path runs on every canonical refresh -- a reader of the subject would believe an unratified, off-by-default feature while the ratified one is executing. SECOND, AND IT IS THE SUBJECT'S OWN OVERCLAIM RATHER THAN A HIDDEN BUG: the docstring promises the guard means 'never swap in a wrong DB', but the implemented check compares CARDINALITY only -- a compensating pair of wrong deletion and wrong addition passes it. The guard is real and worth having; the sentence describing it reaches one step past what it does, which is precisely the failure mode this carding wave keeps finding in prose rather than in code.
